structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E017. The tip is E017: E016's recipe with graph breaks removed, at 6.548 s and 0.7537. The math was meant to be identical, yet accuracy fell 0.70 pp from E016's 0.7607. So a recompile or kernel change alone reshuffles 3-seed accuracy by up to about ±0.4 pp. The true mean of this recipe is probably about 0.756–0.757, and E016's reading was the lucky one. The effective margin over the 0.753 bar is about 0.3 pp in expectation, but only 0.07 pp on the measured tip. Any change that costs accuracy must therefore buy at least 0.3 s to be worth the feasibility risk.

Time model: time ≈ F + V × average pixel fraction. F is about 0.8 s, V is about 7.5 s, and the average pixel fraction is about 0.755. Host overhead is under 1%, so systems levers are exhausted.

Conv cost share by group (MACs, at 32 px): group 1 about 18%, group 2 about 49%, group 3 about 33%.

Estimated trades:
- Swapping the 28 px phase to 24 px: about −0.35 s for −0.1 to −0.25 pp. This is the best trade.
- Adding a 20 px head phase: about −0.15 s for about −0.1 pp.
- Narrowing group 2 to 320: about −0.45 s for −0.3 to −0.6 pp.
- Dropping group 1's third conv: about −0.35 s for −0.2 to −0.4 pp.
- Cutting 1 epoch: about −0.6 s for −0.4 to −0.8 pp.

Weight-decay tweaks change accuracy only within the noise.

forecasts.reason: Pixel fraction drops from 0.755 to 0.694, saving about 0.35 s. The 32 px tail is intact, so the loss is about 0.15 pp, which is within the reshuffle noise.
E017 suggests E016's 0.7607 was a high draw. I expect the 10-seed mean to be about 0.756, which is more than 0.3 pp below 0.7607 and below 0.757.
Cutting 1 epoch saves about 0.6 s but costs 0.4–0.8 pp. With a tip margin of only 0.07 pp, the result most likely lands below 0.753.
Group 2 is about half the MACs, so narrowing it cuts about 7% of time. But CIFAR-100 is width-hungry, so I expect a 0.4–0.6 pp loss, more than the 0.25 pp the hypothesis allows.
This is time-neutral, and the accuracy change should sit inside the reshuffle noise. A +0.2 pp gain over E016's lucky 0.7607 is unlikely.
Removing the conv saves only about 6.5% of conv FLOPs plus some high-resolution elementwise traffic, so time falls about 5%, short of the hypothesis's 8%. Accuracy falls about 0.3 pp.
Pixel fraction falls by only about 0.026, and small maps run inefficiently, so time drops about 2–3%, short of the 4% the hypothesis needs.

cruxes: What is the tip's true multi-seed mean: closer to E016's 0.7607 or E017's 0.7537? That decides whether any accuracy-costing trim is affordable at all.
Is a 24 px step really about 60% of the cost of a 32 px step, or is it near 75% because small maps run inefficiently? That sets how much I029 and I035 save.
Is the accuracy loss from narrowing group 2 or dropping group 1's third conv under 0.3 pp? If so, these FLOP trims beat the epoch dial in seconds per pp.
